questions.q: The equation of the normal to the curve $4 x^2+9 y^2=36$ at the point $P\left(\frac{7 \pi}{4}\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given curve $4 x^2+9 y^2=36$
\frac{x^2}{\left(\frac{36}{4}\right)}+\frac{y^2}{\left(\frac{36}{9}\right)}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1

Equation of normal is $a x \sec \theta-$ by $\operatorname{cosec} \theta=a^2-b^2$
\begin{aligned}
& a^2=a, a= \pm 3, b^2=4, b= \pm 2 \text { and } \theta=\frac{7 \pi}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow 3 x \sec \left(\frac{7 \pi}{4}\right)-2 y \operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{4}\right)=9-4 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 x \sec \left(2 \pi-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-2 y \operatorname{cosec}\left(2 \pi-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=5 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 x \sec \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+2 y \operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=5 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 x(\sqrt{2})+2 y(\sqrt{2})=5 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 \sqrt{2} x+2 \sqrt{2} y-5=0
\end{aligned}

So, equation of normal is $3 \sqrt{2} x+2 \sqrt{2} y-5=0$

$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha^6+\beta^6=(4)\left[(4)^2-3(4)^2\right] \\
